```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
# Fishing in the eastern English Channel (ICES 27.7.d) — report v1.3
# ==============================================================================
# Build with build_eastern_channel.R (fills in the cover page and footers,
# knits, and sets Word to update the fields on opening). The Knit button also
# works once word_build/ exists.
#
# Figures and tables are numbered by Word: captions are set with the chunk
# options fig.cap (figures) and tab.id + tab.cap (tables); cross-references are
# written as Figure \@ref(fig:chunk-label), Table \@ref(tab:table-id) and
# Section \@ref(section-id). Section ids are set on the headings: {#section-id}.
#
# Development note: this report was developed with assistance from Claude
# (Anthropic), which supported code development, data processing, figure
# design and text drafting. All analytical decisions, interpretations and final
# text were reviewed and approved by the author.
# ==============================================================================

# ---- Figure size: never wider than the text width of the MPFF template --------
# officedown inserts figures at their fig.width, without scaling them to the
# page. The text width of the template is 6.5 inch (Letter, 2.5 cm margins).
page_width_in  <- 6.5
page_height_in <- 8.3    # text height minus room for the caption

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo       = FALSE,
  warning    = FALSE,
  message    = FALSE,
  fig.width  = page_width_in,
  fig.height = 4.5,
  dpi        = 200
)

# Chunks with a larger fig.width are scaled down to the text width, keeping
# the height/width ratio; figures higher than the page are cut to page_height_in
knitr::opts_hooks$set(fig.width = function(options) {
  if (options$fig.width > page_width_in) {
    options$fig.height <- options$fig.height * page_width_in / options$fig.width
    options$fig.width  <- page_width_in
  }
  if (options$fig.height > page_height_in) {
    options$fig.height <- page_height_in
  }
  options
})

# ---- Libraries, helper and data-reading functions ---------------------------
source(here::here("R", "Channel_fisheries_functions.R"))
source(here::here("R", "paths.R"))
library(officedown)
library(officer)

# Smaller base font for all plots, to suit the 6.5 inch figure width
# (the figure chunks call theme_bw() and theme_minimal() without a size)
theme_bw      <- function(base_size = 9, ...) ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = base_size, ...)
theme_minimal <- function(base_size = 9, ...) ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = base_size, ...)

# Table rows: 1 pt spacing before and after (instead of the Word default of 5 pt)
flextable::set_flextable_defaults(
  padding.top    = 1,
  padding.bottom = 1,
  line_spacing   = 1
)

# ==============================================================================
# ---- STUDY AREA — set by the build script through params --------------------
# ==============================================================================
# Divisions in the short ICES form ("7.d"); the div_*() functions in
# Channel_fisheries_functions.R convert them to the format of each data source.

study_area <- tibble::tibble(
  div      = params$divisions,
  div_name = params$division_names
)

study_area_name  <- params$study_name
study_area_id    <- paste(gsub("\\.", "", study_area$div), collapse = "_")   # "7d"

# Division used for the finer-scale analyses (identical to the study area here)
focus_div        <- params$focus_div

# Map extents: bounding box of the study divisions plus a buffer (degrees)
study_window_buffer_deg <- 0.5    # GFW study window (KDE, event maps)
map_buffer_deg          <- 1.0    # overview map of the study area

study_divisions_aer <- div_aer(study_area$div)   # "27.7.d"
study_divisions_gfw <- div_gfw(study_area$div)   # "27.7.D"
study_divisions_fdi <- div_fdi(study_area$div)   # "7.D"
focus_div_aer       <- div_aer(focus_div)
focus_div_gfw       <- div_gfw(focus_div)

# Labels for captions and inline text
study_area_lab   <- paste0("ICES ", paste(div_label(study_area$div), collapse = "/"))  # "ICES 27.7.d"
study_area_short <- paste(study_area$div, collapse = "/")                              # "7.d"
study_area_text  <- paste0("ICES division ", div_label(study_area$div),
                           " (", study_area$div_name, ")", collapse = " and ")
focus_div_lab    <- paste0("ICES ", div_label(focus_div))

# ==============================================================================
# ---- Data files (folders are set in R/paths.R) -------------------------------
# ==============================================================================

# AER releases. The newest release is used wherever it has data; the older
# release only adds country x year combinations missing from the newer one
# (here: the UK fleet up to 2020, which left the AER after Brexit).
aer_releases <- list(
  aer2025 = list(
    file            = file.path(inputdir, "STECF 2025-07_AER_data",
                                "STECF_25 07_EU Fleet Economic and Transversal data_fleet segment level.xlsx"),
    label           = "STECF 25-07",
    years           = 2008:2023,     # France absent in 2024
    countries       = NULL,          # NULL = all countries in the file
    effort_sheets   = NULL,
    landings_sheets = NULL
  ),
  aer2021 = list(
    file            = file.path(inputdir, "STECF 2021_08_AER_data",
                                "STECF 21-08 - EU Fleet Economic and Transversal data_fleet segment.xlsx"),
    label           = "STECF 21-08",
    years           = 2008:2020,
    countries       = "GBR",         # only used to add the UK fleet
    effort_sheets   = NULL,
    landings_sheets = NULL
  )
)
aer_priority   <- c("aer2025", "aer2021")    # first = highest priority
aer_source_lab <- paste(vapply(aer_releases[aer_priority], `[[`, "", "label"), collapse = " & ")

fdi_dir     <- file.path(inputdir, "STECF 2025_05_FDI_data")
fdi_files   <- c(
  effort_gearcode = file.path(fdi_dir, "output",
                              "fdi_fishingdays_by_country_sizeclass_gearcode_division_year.csv"),
  catches         = file.path(fdi_dir, "output",
                              "fdi_catches_by_country_sizeclass_gear_division_year.csv")   # optional
)

uk_file     <- file.path(inputdir, "UK data", "SFS24_UK_into_all_ports_non_uk_into_uk_ports_landings_2020_24.xlsx")

gfw_files   <- c(
  effort      = file.path(gfwdir, "gfw_s7_effort.RData"),
  zones       = file.path(gfwdir, "gfw_s6_zones.RData"),
  vessel_meta = file.path(gfwdir, "gfw_s3_vessel_meta.RData")
)
fao_file    <- file.path(spatialdir, "fao_sf.RData")

stock_status_file <- file.path(litdir, "stock_status.xlsx")

out_dir     <- report_out_dir

# One cache folder per study area, so that the 7.d report and the 7.d/7.e/4.c
# report never mix cached objects.
cache_dir   <- file.path(out_dir, "cache", study_area_id)

if (!dir.exists(out_dir))   dir.create(out_dir,   recursive = TRUE)
if (!dir.exists(cache_dir)) dir.create(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# ---- Cache file paths -------------------------------------------------------
div_cache       <- file.path(cache_dir, "cache_divisions.RData")
aer_cache       <- file.path(cache_dir, "cache_aer.RData")
aer_split_cache <- file.path(cache_dir, "cache_aer_split.RData")
fdi_cache       <- file.path(cache_dir, "cache_fdi.RData")

gfw_cache       <- file.path(cache_dir, "cache_gfw.RData")
spatial_cache   <- file.path(cache_dir, "cache_gfw_spatial.RData")

# ---- Spatial objects  -------------------------------------------------------
wind_proj <-
  load_object(filepath = file.path(spatialdir, "EMODNET_windenergy_20260127.RData")) %>%
  sf::st_transform(32630)
mpa_proj <-
  load_object(filepath = file.path(spatialdir, "MPA_N2000.RData")) %>%
  sf::st_transform(32630)

# ---- Study period -----------------------------------------------------------
aer_years_start       <- min(unlist(lapply(aer_releases, `[[`, "years")))   # 2008
aer_years_end         <- max(unlist(lapply(aer_releases, `[[`, "years")))   # 2023
aer_uk_years_end      <- max(aer_releases$aer2021$years)                    # 2020
aer_split_years_start <- 2013   # FDI only available from 2013
gfw_years_start       <- 2013

uk_years                <- 2020:2024
include_channel_islands <- TRUE    # Jersey + Guernsey as country_code "CHI"
# Years used for EU vs UK comparisons (UK share of landings). In 2020 the UK
# figures come from the AER (STECF 21-08), afterwards from MMO.
combined_years          <- 2020:aer_years_end

# ECB annual average exchange rates, GBP per EUR
gbp_per_eur <- c(`2020` = 0.8897, `2021` = 0.8596, `2022` = 0.8528,
                 `2023` = 0.8698, `2024` = 0.8466)

threshold_pct <- 1

# ---- GFW spatial analysis parameters ------------------------------------------
crs_proj    <- 32630   # UTM zone 30N, used for all projected spatial analyses
sigma_all   <- 10000   # KDE bandwidth for the study area (m); 10 km for a single division
sigma_7d    <- 10000   # KDE bandwidth for the focus division (m)
kde_sample  <- 10000   # events sampled per year for KDE

# Spatial concentration metrics for all fleets: "full" = whole study area
# (concentration_full), "focus" = focus division (concentration_7d). Identical
# here, because the study area is a single division.
conc_scope  <- "full"

# AER vs GFW comparison and annual GFW maps: first GFW year left out

gfw_map_years <- (gfw_years_start + 1):max(study_years)

brexit_periods <- list(
  "2014–2020" = 2014:2020,
  "2021–2025" = 2021:2025

kde_flags <- c("FRA", "GBR", "NLD")      # countries in the before/after maps

# The 2012 NLD pelagic anomaly (see helpers-aer) only concerns 27.4.c
if (!"27.4.c" %in% study_divisions_aer) pelagic_anomaly_note <- NULL

# ---- KW-to-GT conversion ----------------------------------------------------
kw_to_gt_ratio <- 0.55

# ---- Country lists ----------------------------------------------------------
report_countries_aer   <- c("DEU", "NLD", "BEL", "FRA", "GBR", "IRL")   # GBR in the AER up to aer_uk_years_end
report_countries_gfw   <- c("DEU", "NLD", "BEL", "FRA", "GBR", "IRL")

# ---- Years without UK (GBR) effort in the AER --------------------------------
# Used to place the asterisks in the effort figures.
gbr_missing_years <- function(effort, years = aer_years_start:aer_years_end) {
  gbr_years <- effort |>
    filter(sub_reg      %in% study_divisions_aer,
           country_code == "GBR",
           totfishdays  > 0) |>
    distinct(year) |>
    pull(year)

  setdiff(years, gbr_years)
}

# ---- Tables without a Total row ---------------------------------------------
# style_ft() formats the last row as a Total row; this wrapper undoes that.
style_ft_plain <- function(ft, ...) {
  n_rows <- nrow(ft$body$dataset)
  style_ft(ft, ...) |>
    flextable::bold(i = n_rows, j = -1, bold = FALSE, part = "body") |>
    flextable::bg(i = n_rows, bg = "white", part = "body")
}

# ---- Number formatting for inline text ------------------------------------------
fmt_n   <- function(x, digits = 0) format(round(x, digits), big.mark = ",", nsmall = digits)
fmt_pct <- function(x) paste0(round(x), "%")

# Range of a vector as text, e.g. "0.53–0.57"; decimal = "," for the Dutch text
fmt_range <- function(x, digits, decimal = ".") {
  lo <- formatC(min(x, na.rm = TRUE), format = "f", digits = digits, decimal.mark = decimal)
  hi <- formatC(max(x, na.rm = TRUE), format = "f", digits = digits, decimal.mark = decimal)
  if (lo == hi) lo else paste0(lo, "–", hi)
}
```

```{r load-divisions, results="hide", message=NA}
# ---- ICES division polygons and map extents ----------------------------------
# fao_sf_division : polygons of the study divisions
# fao_sf_context  : all ICES divisions around the study area (for the maps)
div_objects <- c("fao_sf_division", "fao_sf_context")

if (cache_ok(div_cache, fao_file, div_objects)) {

  msg("Divisions: loading from cache (", format(file.mtime(div_cache), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), ")")
  load(div_cache)

} else {

  msg("Divisions: cache missing, stale or incomplete — reading ", fao_file)
  res <- read_divisions(fao_file, study_divisions_gfw, map_buffer_deg)
  fao_sf_division <- res$fao_sf_division
  fao_sf_context  <- res$fao_sf_context

  save(list = div_objects, file = div_cache)
  msg("Divisions: cache saved → ", div_cache)
  rm(res)
}

# xlim / ylim         : study window for GFW event maps and KDE
# map_xlim / map_ylim : wider window for the study area overview map
extents  <- study_extents(fao_sf_division, study_window_buffer_deg, map_buffer_deg)
xlim     <- extents$xlim
ylim     <- extents$ylim
map_xlim <- extents$map_xlim
map_ylim <- extents$map_ylim
rm(extents)
msg("Study area ", study_area_lab, ": lon ", paste(round(xlim, 2), collapse = " to "),
    ", lat ", paste(round(ylim, 2), collapse = " to "))
```

```{r load-aer, results="hide", message=NA}

# ---- AER effort and landings: all releases in aer_releases --------------------
# aer_effort_bysource / aer_landings_bysource : all releases, stacked (aer_source)
# aer_effort_raw / aer_landings_raw           : per country x year the release
#                                               with the highest priority
# aer_effort_summary, aer_effort_capacity_metric, aer_landings_summary
aer_objects <- c("aer_effort_bysource", "aer_landings_bysource",
                 "aer_effort_raw", "aer_effort_summary",
                 "aer_effort_capacity_metric",
                 "aer_landings_raw", "aer_landings_summary")

aer_source_files <- c(vapply(aer_releases, `[[`, "", "file"), div_cache)

if (cache_ok(aer_cache, aer_source_files, aer_objects)) {

  msg("AER: loading from cache (", format(file.mtime(aer_cache), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), ")")
  load(aer_cache)

} else {

  msg("AER: cache missing, stale or incomplete — reading releases ...")

  # ---- 1. Read each release ---------------------------------------------------
  effort_list   <- list()
  landings_list <- list()

  for (id in aer_priority) {
    rel <- aer_releases[[id]]
    msg("AER: reading ", rel$label, " ...")
    res <- read_aer_release(rel, study_divisions_aer)   # list(effort, landings)
    effort_list[[id]]   <- res$effort
    landings_list[[id]] <- res$landings
  }

  aer_effort_bysource   <- bind_rows(effort_list)
  aer_landings_bysource <- bind_rows(landings_list)

  # ---- 2. Combine: per country x year the release with the highest priority ----
  priority_labels  <- vapply(aer_releases[aer_priority], `[[`, "", "label")
  aer_effort_raw   <- combine_by_priority(aer_effort_bysource,   priority_labels)
  aer_landings_raw <- combine_by_priority(aer_landings_bysource, priority_labels)

  msg("AER combined: source per country (years):")
  aer_effort_raw |>
    group_by(aer_source, country_code) |>
    summarise(years = paste0(min(year), "–", max(year)), .groups = "drop") |>
    print(n = Inf)

  # ---- 3. Summaries -------------------------------------------------------------
  # Fishing days etc. per stratum (vessel_length kept for capacity plots)
  aer_effort_summary <- aer_effort_raw |>
    group_by(aer_source, year, country_code, gear_category, sub_reg, vessel_length) |>
    summarise(
      across(any_of(c("totfishdays", "totseadays", "totkwfishdays", "totgtfishdays")),
             ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  # aer_effort_raw %>% filter(country_code=="NLD") %>% View()
  
  # GT-fishing days where reported; imputed from kW-fishing days otherwise
  aer_effort_capacity_metric <- aer_effort_summary |>
    mutate(
      gt_fishdays_source = case_when(
        totgtfishdays > 0 ~ "GT (reported)",
        totkwfishdays > 0 ~ "GT (imputed from kW)",
        TRUE              ~ "Not available"
      ),
      gt_fishdays_harmonised = case_when(
        totgtfishdays > 0 ~ totgtfishdays,
        totkwfishdays > 0 ~ totkwfishdays * kw_to_gt_ratio,
        TRUE              ~ NA_real_
      )
    )

  aer_landings_summary <- aer_landings_raw |>
    group_by(aer_source, year, country_code, gear_category,
             sub_reg, species_code, species_name) |>
    summarise(
      live_weight_t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE),
      value_euro    = sum(value_euro,    na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  # ---- 4. Save cache --------------------------------------------------------------
  save(list = aer_objects, file = aer_cache)
  msg("AER: cache saved → ", aer_cache)
  rm(effort_list, landings_list, res, rel)
}
```

```{r key-numbers, include=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
# Key numbers used in the text (summaries, results, discussion, conclusions)
# ==============================================================================

# ---- Effort: EU fleets (all years) and all fleets incl. UK (up to 2020) -------------
effort_by_year <- aer_effort_summary |>
  filter(sub_reg %in% study_divisions_aer) |>
  mutate(fleet = if_else(country_code == "GBR", "UK", "EU")) |>
  group_by(year, fleet) |>
  summarise(days = sum(totfishdays, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

eff_eu       <- effort_by_year |> filter(fleet == "EU")
eff_eu_first <- eff_eu$days[eff_eu$year == aer_years_start]
eff_eu_last  <- eff_eu$days[eff_eu$year == aer_years_end]
eff_eu_change_pct <- 100 * (eff_eu_last - eff_eu_first) / eff_eu_first

eff_all <- effort_by_year |>
  filter(year <= aer_uk_years_end) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(days = sum(days), .groups = "drop")
eff_all_first <- eff_all$days[eff_all$year == aer_years_start]
eff_all_ukend <- eff_all$days[eff_all$year == aer_uk_years_end]
eff_all_change_pct <- 100 * (eff_all_ukend - eff_all_first) / eff_all_first

# ---- Effort shares by country, years with UK data -------------------------------------
eff_share <- aer_effort_summary |>
  filter(sub_reg %in% study_divisions_aer,
         year    <= aer_uk_years_end) |>
  mutate(country = if_else(country_code %in% c("FRA", "GBR"), country_code, "Other")) |>
  group_by(country) |>
  summarise(days = sum(totfishdays, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * days / sum(days))

share_fra <- eff_share$pct[eff_share$country == "FRA"]
share_gbr <- eff_share$pct[eff_share$country == "GBR"]
share_oth <- eff_share$pct[eff_share$country == "Other"]

# ---- Seine (SSC/SDN) within bottom trawl/seine (FDI direct splits) ----------------------
if (!is.null(aer_split)) {

  split_direct <- aer_split |>
    filter(split_source == "FDI direct",
           gear_type    != "Unsplit",
           year         %in% aer_split_years_start:aer_years_end)

  seine_share_year <- split_direct |>
    group_by(year) |>
    summarise(pct = 100 * sum(totfishdays_split[gear_type == "Seine (SSC/SDN)"]) /
                          sum(totfishdays_split), .groups = "drop")
  seine_share_range <- fmt_range(seine_share_year$pct, 0)
  otb_share_range   <- fmt_range(100 - seine_share_year$pct, 0)

  seine_by_country <- split_direct |>
    filter(gear_type == "Seine (SSC/SDN)") |>
    group_by(country_code) |>
    summarise(days = sum(totfishdays_split, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(pct = 100 * days / sum(days))
  seine_pct <- function(cty) {
    x <- seine_by_country$pct[seine_by_country$country_code == cty]
    if (length(x) == 0) 0 else x
  }

} else {
  seine_share_range <- "NA"
  otb_share_range   <- "NA"
  seine_pct <- function(cty) NA
}

# ---- Species groups shown in Figures (Other/mixed, key species groups) and Annex B3 ----
# The n_species_groups groups (set in the captions chunk) with the highest landings
# over the whole period (selected gears), in order of total landings; all other
# groups, and species without a group, are combined as "Other".
species_groups_top <- landings_combined |>
  filter(sub_reg       %in% study_divisions_aer,
         gear_category %in% capacity_gears,
         year          %in% aer_years_start:aer_years_end) |>
  mutate(species_group = assign_species_group(species_code_harm, species_name_harm)) |>
  filter(!is.na(species_group)) |>
  group_by(species_group) |>
  summarise(t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(t)) |>
  slice_head(n = n_species_groups) |>
  pull(species_group)

species_group_levels_top <- c(species_groups_top, "Other")

# Species group for the figures and tables: one of species_groups_top, or "Other"
group_species_top <- function(species_code, species_name) {
  g <- assign_species_group(species_code, species_name)
  if_else(!is.na(g) & g %in% species_groups_top, g, "Other")
}

# ---- Landings: top species and UK share --------------------------------------------------
top_species_key <- landings_combined |>
  filter(sub_reg %in% study_divisions_aer,
         year    %in% aer_years_start:aer_years_end) |>
  group_by(species_name_harm) |>
  summarise(t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(t)) |>
  slice_head(n = 3)
top_species_txt <- paste(tolower(top_species_key$species_name_harm), collapse = ", ")

# UK = GBR and Channel Islands, whatever the source: in 2020 the UK landings
# come from the AER (STECF 21-08), from 2021 onwards from MMO.
uk_share <- landings_combined_overlap |>
  filter(sub_reg %in% study_divisions_aer) |>
  mutate(fleet = if_else(country_code %in% c("GBR", "CHI"), "UK", "EU")) |>
  group_by(fleet) |>
  summarise(t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * t / sum(t))
uk_share_pct <- round(uk_share$pct[uk_share$fleet == "UK"])

# ---- Spatial concentration, all fleets -------------------------------------------------------
if (conc_scope == "full") {
  conc_data     <- concentration_full
  conc_area_lab <- study_area_lab
} else {
  conc_data     <- concentration_7d
  conc_area_lab <- focus_div_lab
}

conc_years       <- sort(unique(conc_data$year))
conc_early_years <- head(conc_years, 4)        # first four years
conc_late_years  <- tail(conc_years, 5)        # last five years
conc_early_lab   <- paste0(min(conc_early_years), "–", max(conc_early_years))
conc_late_lab    <- paste0(min(conc_late_years),  "–", max(conc_late_years))

conc_early <- conc_data |> filter(year %in% conc_early_years)
conc_late  <- conc_data |> filter(year %in% conc_late_years)

conc_gini_early  <- fmt_range(conc_early$gini, 2)
conc_gini_late   <- fmt_range(conc_late$gini,  2)
conc_top10_early <- fmt_range(conc_early$top10_pct, 0)
conc_top10_late  <- fmt_range(conc_late$top10_pct,  0)
conc_peak_year   <- conc_data$year[which.max(conc_data$top10_pct)]
conc_peak_top10  <- round(max(conc_data$top10_pct, na.rm = TRUE))
```

<!---CHUNK_PAGEBREAK--->

::: {custom-style="Hheading 1"}
Executive summary
:::

**Background and aim.** The eastern English Channel (`r study_area_lab`) is an intensively exploited fishing ground, with important fisheries for France, the United Kingdom, Belgium and the Netherlands. Over the past decade these fisheries have been shaped by two concurrent forces: changing fish stocks and post-Brexit access restructuring. Against this background, this report was commissioned by Cornelis Vrolijk to provide an objective, evidence-based characterisation of fishing effort, landings and the spatial distribution of the different fleets in the eastern Channel over the period `r aer_years_start`–`r aer_years_end` (AER), `r min(uk_years)`–`r max(uk_years)` (UK landings, MMO), `r aer_split_years_start`–`r aer_years_end` (FDI) and `r gfw_years_start`–`r max(study_years)` (GFW), with particular focus on the flyshoot segment.

**Approach.** Four complementary data sources were integrated:

- STECF Annual Economic Report (AER; STECF 25-07 for the EU fleets and STECF 21-08 for the UK fleet up to `r aer_uk_years_end`), providing official fishing effort and landings by fleet segment;
- UK landings data from the Marine Management Organisation (MMO), covering UK and Channel Islands vessels, which are absent from the AER after `r aer_uk_years_end`;
- STECF Fisheries Dependent Information database (FDI, STECF 25-10), used to disaggregate the AER bottom trawl/seine category into conventional otter trawl (OTB) and seine (SSC/SDN) gears;
- Global Fishing Watch (GFW) AIS-derived fishing event data, used for the spatial analysis of effort distribution and concentration.

**Key findings.** Total fishing effort of the EU fleets in the eastern Channel changed from `r fmt_n(eff_eu_first)` fishing days in `r aer_years_start` to `r fmt_n(eff_eu_last)` in `r aer_years_end` (`r fmt_pct(eff_eu_change_pct)`), with the contraction of the French otter trawl fleet as an important driver. France dominates the effort picture: between `r aer_years_start` and `r aer_uk_years_end` France accounted for `r fmt_pct(share_fra)` of the AER fishing days, the UK for `r fmt_pct(share_gbr)` and all other countries together for `r fmt_pct(share_oth)`. The dominant gears are bottom trawl/seine, dredge, gillnet, pot/trap and Other/mixed; French bottom trawl/seine and gillnet effort has declined over time. Within the bottom trawl/seine category, seine gears (SSC/SDN) account for `r seine_share_range`% of the fishing days. The Dutch flyshoot fleet, while small in absolute terms, is the main seine fleet in the area, with `r fmt_pct(seine_pct("NLD"))` of the seine days, against `r fmt_pct(seine_pct("FRA"))` for France and `r fmt_pct(seine_pct("GBR"))` for the UK.

Landings from the eastern Channel are dominated by pelagic fish (mainly the Netherlands, Germany, the UK and France) and scallops (France and the UK); the species with the highest landings over the whole period are `r top_species_txt`. Roundfish and flatfish landings have declined sharply, while scallop landings have increased since 2016. Cuttlefish and squid landings have increased but remain small relative to other landings. Over `r min(combined_years)`–`r max(combined_years)`, UK and Channel Islands vessels accounted for `r uk_share_pct`% of the landings from the eastern Channel, with a clearly different profile, dominated by shellfish (whelk, scallops, cockles and crab) taken with pots and traps and dredges.

**Spatial patterns.** The GFW data show persistent fishing hotspots in the Baie de Seine and the Pas de Calais, reflecting the concentration of bottom trawl and dredge activities. French effort is spread broadly over the area, UK effort is concentrated in the northern part and Dutch effort in the central-eastern part of 27.7.d. After Brexit, French effort became more concentrated in the Baie de Seine, UK effort became slightly more diffuse and Dutch effort slightly more concentrated in the central-eastern part of 27.7.d. The spatial concentration of fishing effort of all fleets combined increased, from a Gini coefficient of `r conc_gini_early` in `r conc_early_lab` to `r conc_gini_late` in `r conc_late_lab`, and from `r conc_top10_early`% to `r conc_top10_late`% of the total effort in the top-10% of grid cells, with a slight peak around 2020 (post-Brexit access uncertainty and COVID-19).

**Conclusions.** The fisheries in the eastern Channel show a long-term decline in fishing effort, mainly through the contraction of the French otter trawl fleet; France remains the country with the highest effort in the area. The composition of the landings is changing: scallops and cephalopods are increasing, flatfish and roundfish are declining, and pelagic fish remain relatively stable and high. The Dutch flyshoot fleet occupies a small but stable position within this system as the main seine fleet. After Brexit, the distribution of the national fleets has changed and fishing effort has become somewhat more concentrated. The combination of AER, MMO, FDI and GFW data provides a multi-source baseline to compare the different fleets in the eastern Channel and to monitor future changes in fleet composition and spatial distribution. Quantifying the area swept per vessel-day using gear-specific swept-area coefficients is recommended as a priority next step for translating the effort trends into ecologically meaningful impact metrics.

::: {custom-style="Hheading 1"}
Nederlandse samenvatting
:::

**Achtergrond en doel.** Het oostelijk deel van het Engelse Kanaal (`r study_area_lab`) is een intensief bevist gebied, met belangrijke visserijen voor Frankrijk, het Verenigd Koninkrijk, België en Nederland. In het afgelopen decennium zijn deze visserijen beïnvloed door twee gelijktijdige ontwikkelingen: veranderende visbestanden en herstructurering van de toegang na Brexit. In dit kader is dit rapport in opdracht van Cornelis Vrolijk opgesteld. Het doel is een objectieve, op feiten gebaseerde beschrijving van de visserij-inspanning, aanvoer en ruimtelijke verdeling van de verschillende vloten in het oostelijk Kanaal over de periode `r aer_years_start`–`r aer_years_end` (AER), `r min(uk_years)`–`r max(uk_years)` (Britse aanvoer, MMO), `r aer_split_years_start`–`r aer_years_end` (FDI) en `r gfw_years_start`–`r max(study_years)` (GFW), met bijzondere aandacht voor het flyshoot-segment.

**Aanpak.** Vier complementaire databronnen zijn gecombineerd:

- STECF Annual Economic Report (AER; STECF 25-07 voor de EU-vloten en STECF 21-08 voor de Britse vloot tot en met `r aer_uk_years_end`), met officiële gegevens over visserij-inspanning en aanvoer per vlootsegment;
- aanvoergegevens van de Britse Marine Management Organisation (MMO) voor Britse vaartuigen en vaartuigen van de Kanaaleilanden, die na `r aer_uk_years_end` niet meer in de AER zijn opgenomen;
- STECF Fisheries Dependent Information-database (FDI, STECF 25-10), gebruikt om de AER-categorie bodemtrawl/zegen te splitsen in conventionele bordenvisserij (OTB) en zegenvisserij (SSC/SDN);
- AIS-gegevens van Global Fishing Watch (GFW) over visserij-activiteiten, gebruikt voor de ruimtelijke analyse van de verdeling en concentratie van de inspanning.

**Belangrijkste bevindingen.** De totale visserij-inspanning van de EU-vloten in het oostelijk Kanaal veranderde van `r fmt_n(eff_eu_first)` visdagen in `r aer_years_start` naar `r fmt_n(eff_eu_last)` in `r aer_years_end` (`r fmt_pct(eff_eu_change_pct)`), met de inkrimping van de Franse bordenvisserij als belangrijke oorzaak. Frankrijk domineert het inspanningsbeeld: in `r aer_years_start`–`r aer_uk_years_end` was Frankrijk goed voor `r fmt_pct(share_fra)` van de AER-visdagen, het VK voor `r fmt_pct(share_gbr)` en de overige landen samen voor `r fmt_pct(share_oth)`. De belangrijkste vistuigen zijn bodemtrawl/zegen, dreg, staand want, potten/fuiken en overig/gemengd; de Franse inspanning met bodemtrawl/zegen en staand want is in de loop van de tijd afgenomen. Binnen de categorie bodemtrawl/zegen is `r seine_share_range`% van de visdagen zegenvisserij (SSC/SDN). De Nederlandse flyshootvloot is in absolute termen klein, maar is de belangrijkste zegenvloot in het gebied, met `r fmt_pct(seine_pct("NLD"))` van de zegendagen; Frankrijk heeft `r fmt_pct(seine_pct("FRA"))` en het VK `r fmt_pct(seine_pct("GBR"))`.

De aanvoer uit het oostelijk Kanaal wordt gedomineerd door pelagische vis (vooral Nederland, Duitsland, het VK en Frankrijk) en sint-jakobsschelpen (Frankrijk en het VK). De aanvoer van rondvis en platvis is sterk gedaald, terwijl de aanvoer van sint-jakobsschelpen sinds 2016 is toegenomen. De aanvoer van zeekat en pijlinktvis is toegenomen, maar blijft klein vergeleken met de overige aanvoer. In `r min(combined_years)`–`r max(combined_years)` waren Britse vaartuigen en vaartuigen van de Kanaaleilanden goed voor `r uk_share_pct`% van de aanvoer uit het oostelijk Kanaal, met een duidelijk ander profiel: vooral schelp- en schaaldieren (wulken, sint-jakobsschelpen, kokkels en krab), gevangen met potten en fuiken en dreggen.

**Ruimtelijke patronen.** De GFW-gegevens laten persistente visserijhotspots zien in de Baie de Seine en het Nauw van Calais, waar de bodemtrawl- en dregvisserij geconcentreerd is. De Franse inspanning is breed over het gebied verspreid, de Britse inspanning is geconcentreerd in het noordelijk deel en de Nederlandse inspanning in het centraal-oostelijk deel van 27.7.d. Na Brexit is de Franse inspanning sterker geconcentreerd in de Baie de Seine, is de Britse inspanning iets meer verspreid geraakt en de Nederlandse inspanning iets meer geconcentreerd in het centraal-oostelijk deel van 27.7.d. De ruimtelijke concentratie van de visserij-inspanning van alle vloten samen nam toe, van een Gini-coëfficiënt van `r fmt_range(conc_early$gini, 2, ",")` in `r conc_early_lab` naar `r fmt_range(conc_late$gini, 2, ",")` in `r conc_late_lab`, en van `r conc_top10_early`% naar `r conc_top10_late`% van de totale inspanning in de 10% meest beviste rastercellen, met een lichte piek rond 2020 (onzekerheid over de toegang na Brexit en COVID-19).

**Conclusies.** De visserij in het oostelijk Kanaal laat een langdurige afname van de visserij-inspanning zien, vooral door de inkrimping van de Franse bordenvisserij; Frankrijk blijft het land met de hoogste inspanning in het gebied. De samenstelling van de aanvoer verandert: sint-jakobsschelpen en inktvissen nemen toe, platvis en rondvis nemen af, en pelagische vis blijft relatief stabiel en hoog. De Nederlandse flyshootvloot neemt binnen dit systeem een kleine maar stabiele positie in als belangrijkste zegenvloot. Na Brexit is de verspreiding van de nationale vloten veranderd en is de visserij-inspanning iets meer geconcentreerd geraakt. De combinatie van AER-, MMO-, FDI- en GFW-gegevens biedt een basis uit meerdere bronnen om de verschillende vloten in het oostelijk Kanaal te vergelijken en om toekomstige veranderingen in vlootsamenstelling en ruimtelijke verdeling te volgen. Het kwantificeren van de bestreken oppervlakte per visdag via vistuig-specifieke *swept area*-coëfficiënten wordt aanbevolen als prioritaire volgende stap.

# Introduction {#intro}

## Background

This study looks into the international fisheries developments in the eastern English Channel in the past 15 years. Over this period there has been an increase in the fisheries for squid and cuttlefish in the Channel (and more recently also in the southern North Sea). This change in fishing patterns has come under increasing public and media scrutiny, including critical coverage in the Netherlands (e.g. Follow the Money). This study attempts to provide a thorough knowledge base on the fisheries in the eastern Channel using data from different sources: 1) STECF Annual Economic Report (AER; STECF 21-08 and 25-07; STECF, 2021, 2025a), 2) UK landings data `r min(uk_years)`–`r max(uk_years)` (MMO, 2025), 3) STECF Fisheries Dependent Information (FDI; STECF, 2025b) and 4) Global Fishing Watch data (https://globalfishingwatch.org). The aim is to provide an objective, evidence-based assessment of the fisheries development in terms of effort and catches of the fleets operating in the eastern Channel, their spatial distribution, and the available scientific literature on those fisheries.

The report was commissioned by the Cornelis Vrolijk company (https://www.cornelisvrolijk.eu) and executed by Martin Pastoors Fish & Fisheries.

## Objectives

- To quantify trends in fishing effort and landings in the eastern Channel (2008/2013–present) using official STECF (AER) and MMO statistics.
- To characterise the spatial distribution and concentration of fishing effort in the eastern Channel, and the changes after Brexit, using GFW AIS data.
- To compile a scientifically grounded overview of the fisheries in the Channel, with particular focus on sustainability, ecosystem effects and the positioning of the flyshoot fishery.

## Study area and scope {#study-area}

The study covers `r study_area_text`, which will be called the "study area" in this report (Figure \@ref(fig:study-area-map)). The western Channel (27.7.e) and the southern North Sea (27.4.c) are not included in this version of the report.

```{r study-area-map, fig.height=6.5, fig.width=8, fig.cap=cap[["study-area-map"]]}

# ---- Study area map: ICES divisions, countries and water depth ---------------
# Depth: NOAA ETOPO 2022 global relief model at 1 arc-minute (~1.8 km),
# downloaded once with marmap::getNOAA.bathy() (needs an internet connection
# and the marmap package: install.packages("marmap")).
# The depth grid is stored in cache_map.RData, together with the map window
# it was downloaded for; it is downloaded again when map_xlim / map_ylim change.
# ICES division outlines: fao_sf_context (load-divisions chunk).
# The map window (map_xlim / map_ylim) follows from the study divisions plus
# map_buffer_deg (setup); uncomment the two lines below to set it by hand.
#
# EEZ boundaries: Marine Regions World EEZ v12 boundary lines (Flanders Marine
# Institute, 2023). Either set eez_file to a local copy of the boundaries
# layer (e.g. "eez_boundaries_v12.shp" from https://www.marineregions.org/downloads.php),
# or leave it NULL to download the layer once with the mregions2 package
# (install.packages("mregions2")). Stored in cache_eez.RData.

map_cache      <- file.path(cache_dir, "cache_map.RData")
# map_xlim       <- c(-8, 3)         # longitude range of the map
# map_ylim       <- c(47.5, 51.3)    # latitude range of the map
show_windfarms <- TRUE             # draw operational/approved wind farms
eez_cache      <- file.path(cache_dir, "cache_eez.RData")
eez_file       <- NULL             # optional local EEZ boundaries file (shp/gpkg)

# ---- Depth grid (NOAA ETOPO) ----------------------------------------------------
bathy_df    <- NULL
map_cache_ok <- FALSE

if (file.exists(map_cache)) {
  load(map_cache)   # bathy_df, bathy_xlim, bathy_ylim
  # Only valid if it was downloaded for the same map window
  map_cache_ok <- exists("bathy_xlim") && exists("bathy_ylim") &&
                  isTRUE(all.equal(bathy_xlim, map_xlim)) &&
                  isTRUE(all.equal(bathy_ylim, map_ylim))
  if (map_cache_ok) {
    msg("Map: depth grid loaded from cache")
  } else {
    msg("Map: map window has changed — depth grid is downloaded again")
    bathy_df <- NULL
  }
}

if (!map_cache_ok) {

  msg("Map: downloading depth grid from NOAA ...")
  bathy_df <- tryCatch({
    b <- marmap::getNOAA.bathy(lon1 = map_xlim[1] - 0.5, lon2 = map_xlim[2] + 0.5,
                               lat1 = map_ylim[1] - 0.5, lat2 = map_ylim[2] + 0.5,
                               resolution = 1)
    marmap::fortify.bathy(b)                 # columns x (lon), y (lat), z (m)
  }, error = function(e) {
    msg("Map: depth download failed (", conditionMessage(e),
        "); the map is drawn without depth and the download is retried next knit.")
    NULL
  })

  if (!is.null(bathy_df)) {
    bathy_xlim <- map_xlim
    bathy_ylim <- map_ylim
    save(bathy_df, bathy_xlim, bathy_ylim, file = map_cache)
    msg("Map: cache saved → ", map_cache)
  }
}

# ---- ICES divisions in the map window --------------------------------------------
# fao_sf_context (load-divisions) holds all divisions around the study area
ices_div_map <- fao_sf_context

# ---- EEZ boundaries ------------------------------------------------------------
if (file.exists(eez_cache)) {

  load(eez_cache)   # eez_lines

} else {

  eez_raw <- tryCatch({
    if (!is.null(eez_file)) {
      msg("Map: reading EEZ boundaries from ", eez_file)
      sf::st_read(eez_file, quiet = TRUE)
    } else {
      msg("Map: downloading EEZ boundaries from Marine Regions (first knit only) ...")
      mregions2::mrp_get("eez_boundaries")
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    msg("Map: EEZ boundaries not available (", conditionMessage(e),
        "); the map is drawn without EEZs and this is retried next knit.")
    NULL
  })

  eez_lines <- NULL
  if (!is.null(eez_raw)) {
    s2_old <- sf::sf_use_s2()
    sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)
    eez_bbox <- sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = map_xlim[1] - 1, xmax = map_xlim[2] + 1,
                                            ymin = map_ylim[1] - 1, ymax = map_ylim[2] + 1),
                                          crs = 4326))
    eez_lines <- eez_raw |>
      sf::st_transform(4326) |>
      sf::st_make_valid() |>
      sf::st_intersection(eez_bbox) |>
      dplyr::select(geometry)
    sf::sf_use_s2(s2_old)
    rm(eez_raw)
    save(eez_lines, file = eez_cache)
    msg("Map: EEZ cache saved → ", eez_cache)
  }
}

# EEZ names: fixed label positions (lon, lat); adjust if labels overlap.
# Labels outside the map window are dropped below.
eez_labels <- tibble::tribble(
  ~label,              ~lon,   ~lat,
  "UK EEZ",            -1.6,   50.30,
  "French EEZ",        -0.9,   49.80,
  "UK EEZ",             1.9,   52.30,
  "Belgian EEZ",        2.75,  51.45,
  "Dutch EEZ",          4.0,   52.85,
  "German EEZ",         6.6,   53.70,
  "Jersey / Guernsey", -2.6,   49.60
) |>
  filter(between(lon, map_xlim[1] + 0.2, map_xlim[2] - 0.2),
         between(lat, map_ylim[1] + 0.1, map_ylim[2] - 0.1))

# ---- Depth classes ------------------------------------------------------------
depth_breaks <- c(0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 150, 200, Inf)
depth_labels <- c("0–20", "20–40", "40–60", "60–80", "80–100",
                  "100–150", "150–200", "> 200")
depth_colours <- setNames(
  colorRampPalette(c("#EAF3FA", "#9CC3E0", "#4A8BBF", "#1F4E79"))(length(depth_labels)),
  depth_labels)

depth_df <- if (!is.null(bathy_df)) {
  bathy_df |>
    filter(z < 0) |>
    mutate(depth       = -z,
           depth_class = cut(depth, breaks = depth_breaks, labels = depth_labels,
                             include.lowest = TRUE))
} else NULL

# ---- Layers in geographic coordinates (WGS84) ---------------------------------
study_div_map <- ices_div_map |>
  filter(division %in% study_divisions_gfw)

# Labels of the study divisions: by default at a point inside each division;
# positions in study_div_label_pos (lon, lat) replace that where given.
study_div_label_pos <- tibble::tribble(
  ~division,  ~lon,   ~lat,
  "27.7.D",    0.6,   50.25,
  "27.7.E",   -4.3,   49.55
)

study_div_labels <- suppressWarnings(sf::st_point_on_surface(study_div_map)) |>
  mutate(lon = sf::st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1],
         lat = sf::st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2]) |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  dplyr::select(division, lon, lat)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(study_div_label_pos))) {
  hit <- study_div_labels$division == study_div_label_pos$division[i]
  study_div_labels$lon[hit] <- study_div_label_pos$lon[i]
  study_div_labels$lat[hit] <- study_div_label_pos$lat[i]
}
other_div_labels <- ices_div_map |>
  filter(!division %in% study_divisions_gfw) |>
  sf::st_point_on_surface() |>
  suppressWarnings() |>
  mutate(lon = sf::st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1],
         lat = sf::st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2]) |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(between(lon, map_xlim[1] + 0.3, map_xlim[2] - 0.3),
         between(lat, map_ylim[1] + 0.2, map_ylim[2] - 0.2))

country_labels <- tibble::tribble(
  ~label,            ~lon,  ~lat,
  "United Kingdom",  -1.6,  52.4,
  "France",           1.5,  48.6,
  "Belgium",          4.6,  50.6,
  "Netherlands",      5.7,  52.4,
  "Germany",          7.2,  53.2,
  "Channel Islands", -2.4,  49.15
) |>
  filter(between(lon, map_xlim[1] + 0.3, map_xlim[2] - 0.3),
         between(lat, map_ylim[1] + 0.1, map_ylim[2] - 0.1))

windfarms_map <- if (show_windfarms && exists("wind_proj")) {
  wind_proj |>
    filter(STATUS %in% c("Approved", "Production")) |>
    sf::st_transform(4326)
} else NULL

# ---- Plot ---------------------------------------------------------------------
p_map <- ggplot()

if (!is.null(depth_df)) {
  p_map <- p_map +
    geom_raster(data = depth_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = depth_class)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = depth_colours, name = "Depth (m)", drop = FALSE)
}

p_map <- p_map +
  geom_sf(data = ices_div_map, fill = NA, colour = "grey45",
          linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dotted")

if (!is.null(eez_lines)) {
  p_map <- p_map +
    geom_sf(data = eez_lines, colour = "#8B1A1A", linewidth = 0.45,
            linetype = "dashed")
}

if (!is.null(windfarms_map)) {
  p_map <- p_map +
    geom_sf(data = windfarms_map, fill = "grey20", colour = "grey20",
            linewidth = 0.1, alpha = 0.6)
}

p_map <- p_map +
  geom_sf(data = world, fill = "grey88", colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_sf(data = study_div_map, fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = other_div_labels, aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = division),
            size = 2.4, colour = "grey35") +
  geom_label(data = study_div_labels, aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = division),
             size = 3.2, fontface = "bold", fill = alpha("white", 0.8),
             label.size = 0) +
  geom_text(data = country_labels, aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = label),
            size = 3, fontface = "italic", colour = "grey25") +
  { if (!is.null(eez_lines))
      geom_text(data = eez_labels, aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = label),
                size = 2.6, colour = "#8B1A1A") } +
  coord_sf(crs = 4326, xlim = map_xlim, ylim = map_ylim, expand = FALSE) +
  labs(title    = paste0("Study area: ", study_area_name),
       subtitle = paste0(study_area_lab, " (bold outline)"),
       caption  = paste0("Depth: NOAA ETOPO 2022 (1 arc-minute). Dotted grey lines: other ICES divisions.",
                         if (!is.null(eez_lines))
                           " Dashed red lines: EEZ boundaries (Marine Regions, World EEZ v12).",
                         if (!is.null(windfarms_map))
                           " Dark grey: offshore wind farms (operational or approved)."),
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#EAF3FA"),
        panel.grid       = element_line(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2),
        legend.position  = "bottom",
        plot.caption     = element_text(size = 7, colour = "grey40")) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1))

p_map
```

The period of analysis is `r aer_years_start`–`r aer_years_end` for effort and landings trends (AER; data for 2024 were not available for France and 2024 has therefore been left out; the UK fleet is included up to `r aer_uk_years_end`), `r min(uk_years)`–`r max(uk_years)` for UK landings (MMO), and `r gfw_years_start`–`r max(study_years)` for the spatial analysis (GFW).

# Material & Methods {#methods}

This report combines four data sources, each covering a different period and providing different information. Figure \@ref(fig:data-overview) gives an overview: the AER provides the long-term series of effort and landings, the MMO data add the landings of the UK and Channel Islands fleets after `r aer_uk_years_end`, the FDI data are used only to split the AER bottom trawl/seine category into otter trawl and seine, and the GFW data are used only for the spatial analysis. The sources are described in detail in Sections \@ref(aer-data) to \@ref(gfw-data).

```{r data-overview, fig.height=10, fig.width=9, fig.cap=cap[["data-overview"]]}

# ---- Timeline rows -------------------------------------------------------------
# One row per AER release (in priority order), then FDI, MMO and GFW.
# The description of each AER release follows from its country selection.
aer_rows <- list()
for (id in aer_priority) {
  rel <- aer_releases[[id]]
  fleets <- if (is.null(rel$countries)) {
    "EU fleets"
  } else {
    paste(paste(rel$countries, collapse = ", "), "fleet")
  }
  aer_rows[[id]] <- tibble::tibble(
    source = paste0("AER ", sub("^STECF ", "", rel$label)),   # e.g. "AER 25-07"
    label  = paste0("AER (", rel$label, ")\nEffort and landings, ", fleets),
    start  = min(rel$years),
    end    = max(rel$years)
  )
}

data_timeline <- bind_rows(
  arrange(bind_rows(aer_rows), source),
  tibble::tribble(
    ~source, ~label,                                                ~start,                 ~end,
    "MMO",   "MMO (UK)\nLandings, UK and Channel Islands",          min(uk_years),          max(uk_years),
    "FDI",   "FDI (STECF 25-10)\nGear split key (OTB vs SSC/SDN)",  aer_split_years_start,  aer_years_end,
    "GFW",   "GFW (AIS)\nSpatial distribution of effort",           gfw_years_start,        max(study_years)
  )
) |>
  mutate(label = factor(label, levels = rev(label)))

# Colours: shades of blue for the AER releases, fixed colours for the others
aer_sources <- sort((unique(bind_rows(aer_rows)$source)))
data_source_colours <- c(
  setNames(colorRampPalette(c("#2E5A88", "#8FB3D9"))(max(2, length(aer_sources)))[seq_along(sort(aer_sources))],
           aer_sources),
  FDI = "#76B7B2", MMO = "#59A14F", GFW = "#F28E2B"
)

# Years in which UK landings come from MMO instead of the AER
uk_mmo_years <- uk_years[uk_years > aer_uk_years_end]

# ---- Top panel: timeline ----------------------------------------------------
p_time <- ggplot(data_timeline) +
  # annotate("rect",
  #          xmin = min(uk_mmo_years), xmax = max(uk_mmo_years),
  #          ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "grey85", alpha = 0.6) +
  # annotate("text", x = mean(uk_mmo_years), y = Inf,
  #          label = "UK landings from MMO", vjust = 1.2, size = 2.6,
  #          colour = "grey30") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = aer_uk_years_end + 0.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  annotate("text", x = aer_uk_years_end + 0.5, y = -Inf, label = "End of Brexit transition",
           hjust = 1, vjust = -0.3, size = 2.6, colour = "grey30") +
  # +/- 0.45 so that a bar covers the whole of its first and last year
  geom_linerange(aes(y = label, xmin = start - 0.45, xmax = end + 0.45,
                     colour = source),
                 linewidth = 9) +
  # period label made in the data: a non-ASCII character inside aes() fails
  # when ggplot2 builds its default labels on Windows
  geom_text(data = data_timeline |> mutate(period_lab = paste0(start, "\u2013", end)),
            aes(y = label, x = (start + end) / 2, label = period_lab),
            colour = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = data_source_colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = aer_years_start:max(study_years),
                     limits = c(aer_years_start - 0.5, max(study_years) + 0.5),
                     expand = expansion(0)) +
  labs(subtitle = "Period covered and role in this report", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5),
        axis.text.y        = element_text(size = 8, hjust = 1),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

# ---- Bottom panel: content matrix -------------------------------------------
# One AER column: the releases share the same structure and resolution.
dims <- c("Fleets", "Effort", "Landings", "Gear", "Vessel size",
          "Spatial resolution", "Time resolution")

content_colours <- c(AER = unname(data_source_colours[aer_sources[1]]),
                     data_source_colours[c("FDI", "MMO", "GFW")])

data_content <- tibble::tribble(

  mutate(source    = factor(source, levels = names(content_colours)),

p_content <- ggplot(data_content, aes(x = source, y = dimension, fill = status)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = text), size = 2.4, lineheight = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Full = "#A8D5BA", Partial = "#F6D58E", None = "#E8A3A3"),
                    name = "Coverage") +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  labs(subtitle = "Content and resolution", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x     = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10,
                                       colour = unname(content_colours)),
        panel.grid      = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom")

p_time / p_content +
  plot_layout(heights = c(1.3, 2.3)) +
  plot_annotation(title = "Data sources used in this report",
                  theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")))
```

## STECF AER data (effort and landings trends) {#aer-data}

The Annual Economic Report (AER) data were obtained from two STECF data releases (*EU Fleet Economic and Transversal data, fleet segment level*): STECF 25-07 (STECF, 2025a), covering the EU Member States for `r min(aer_releases$aer2025$years)`–`r max(aer_releases$aer2025$years)`, and STECF 21-08 (STECF, 2021), the last release that includes the United Kingdom, covering `r min(aer_releases$aer2021$years)`–`r max(aer_releases$aer2021$years)`. The 25-07 release is used for every country × year combination it contains; the 21-08 release only adds the UK fleet. The AER provides fishing effort (fishing days, sea days, kW-days, GT-days) and landed weight and value by fleet segment (country × fishing technique × vessel length class), disaggregated by FAO division.

The AER analyses in this report cover the period `r aer_years_start`–`r aer_years_end`. The end year of `r aer_years_end` reflects the absence of French effort and landings data for 2024 in the current STECF 25-07 release. The AER does not distinguish between bottom trawl and seine fisheries; they are reported as a combined category.

After `r aer_uk_years_end` the AER no longer contains data for the United Kingdom. UK landings for the later years were therefore obtained separately from the UK Marine Management Organisation (Section \@ref(uk-data)). No UK effort data were available for the years after `r aer_uk_years_end`, so from `r aer_uk_years_end + 1` onwards the effort figures cover EU fleets only; years without UK effort are marked with an asterisk in the effort figures.

### Vessel length classes

The AER reports effort and landings by vessel length class (VLC), defined by overall length (LOA) in metres. Six standard classes are used throughout this report, as defined in the STECF fleet data collection framework (Table \@ref(tab:vlc-table)).

```{r vlc-table, tab.id="vlc-table", tab.cap=cap[["vlc-table"]]}
tibble::tibble(
  `Code`              = c("VL0010","VL1012","VL1218","VL1824","VL2440","VL40XX"),
  `Length range (m)`  = c("< 10","10–12","12–18","18–24","24–40","> 40"),
  `Typical vessel type` = c(
    "Small inshore vessels (outboard/inboard motor)",
    "Small coastal vessels",
    "Medium coastal/demersal vessels",
    "Medium offshore vessels, beam trawlers, flyshoot",
    "Large demersal and pelagic trawlers",
    "Freezer trawlers"
  )
) |>
  flextable::flextable() |>
  style_ft_plain(font_size = 9)
```

### Species groups {#species-groups}

Landings in the AER are reported at the individual species level using FAO 3-alpha species codes. For summary figures and tables, individual species are aggregated into ecologically and commercially meaningful species groups. The grouping was applied using FAO 3-alpha codes as the primary key (reliable and consistent across Member States) with species name pattern matching as a fallback. Table \@ref(tab:spp-group-table) lists the species groups used and the main constituent species.

## UK landings data (MMO) {#uk-data}

UK landings were obtained from the dataset underlying the UK Sea Fisheries Statistics 2024 (MMO, 2025), covering landings by UK vessels into all ports and landings by non-UK vessels into UK ports for `r min(uk_years)`–`r max(uk_years)`. The dataset reports monthly landings by vessel nationality, ICES division and statistical rectangle, port of landing, vessel length group, gear category and species, as live weight, landed weight and first-sale value (GBP).

**Selection.** Only vessels of UK nationality (England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland) were retained, together with vessels from Jersey and Guernsey, which are reported separately as Channel Islands (CHI). Landings by non-UK vessels into UK ports were excluded, because these are already included in the AER data of the respective flag states. The data were restricted to `r study_area_lab`.

**Harmonisation with the AER.** UK vessel length groups were mapped onto the AER vessel length classes (Table \@ref(tab:vlc-table)) using the lower bound of each length group. UK gear categories were mapped onto the AER gear categories as shown in Table \@ref(tab:uk-gear-map-table). The original UK gear categories were retained in addition; unlike the AER, they distinguish demersal trawls from demersal seines. Species are coded with FAO 3-alpha codes in both sources, but some species are reported under different codes. Horse mackerel (HOM/JAX), cuttlefish (CTC/CTL), monkfish (ANF/MON/MNZ), squids (SQC/SQR/SQZ) and skates and rays (RJX/SKA) were therefore harmonised to a common code before species grouping (Section \@ref(species-groups)). Live weight was used throughout, consistent with the AER. Values were converted from GBP to EUR using annual average ECB exchange rates.

**Use and limitations.** The MMO data cover landings only. They are added only for the country × year combinations that are not in the AER, i.e. from `r aer_uk_years_end + 1` onwards; for `r aer_uk_years_end` and earlier the UK landings come from the AER (STECF 21-08), so nothing is counted twice. UK landings before and after `r aer_uk_years_end + 1` therefore come from different sources, which may differ somewhat in coverage. UK effort is only available from the AER, up to `r aer_uk_years_end`. Spatial attribution may differ slightly between sources: UK landings are attributed to the reported rectangle and division, while AER landings by sub-region are compiled by Member States from logbook and sales-note data.

```{r uk-gear-map-table, tab.id="uk-gear-map-table", tab.cap=cap[["uk-gear-map-table"]]}
tibble::tibble(
  `UK gear category (MMO)` = c("Demersal trawls", "Demersal seine", "Beam trawl",
                               "Dredge", "Drift and fixed nets",
                               "Handlines, Longlines", "Pots and traps",
                               "Pelagic seine",
                               "Pelagic trawls, Other mobile/passive gears, Unknown"),
  `AER gear category`      = c("Bottom trawl/seine", "Bottom trawl/seine", "Beam trawl",
                               "Dredge", "Gillnet",
                               "Handline/rod", "Pot/trap",
                               "Purse seine",
                               "Other/mixed")
) |>
  flextable::flextable() |>
  style_ft_plain(font_size = 9)
```

## STECF FDI data: limitations and use as gear-splitting key {#fdi-data}

The STECF Fisheries Dependent Information (FDI) dataset was obtained for the study area and period. Unfortunately, the FDI Landings table is EU-aggregated (no country breakdown), and the Effort and Catches tables suffer from substantial confidentiality suppression in many strata. In addition, the spatial FDI tables were not available on the STECF website at the time of analysis. Therefore, the FDI data have not been used as the main source of data for the report.

Despite these limitations, the FDI Effort table retains one piece of information not available in the AER data: **gear code at the FAO level** (e.g. OTB, OTT, SSC, SDN, PTB). The AER combines all of these into a single Bottom trawl/seine category, which conflates conventional otter trawl (OTB) with Danish/Scottish seine (SSC/SDN), two gears with very different fishing patterns and fleet compositions. The FDI gear-code information is therefore used to disaggregate the AER Bottom trawl/seine category, as described below.

**Splitting approach.** For each stratum (year, country, vessel length class, division), the share of each gear code within the Bottom trawl/seine total was computed from the FDI Effort table. This proportional split key was then applied to the corresponding AER fishing days, so that the total days in each stratum are conserved exactly. Shares in the FDI strata are rescaled to sum to 1 within each stratum, which handles any within-stratum confidentiality suppression transparently, although it does not account for seasonal dynamics.

**Coverage and fallback rules.** FDI data are used for `r aer_split_years_start`–`r aer_years_end` only. Strata with no FDI coverage (primarily IRL, DNK, and some BEL and DEU strata where FDI reported zero or suppressed days) are assigned a pooled fallback split key derived from the FDI data aggregated across all available years and countries, stratified by vessel length class.

**Limitations.** Countries for which FDI coverage is sparse (IRL, DNK, DEU) receive a pooled fleet-average split that may not reflect their actual gear mix. Results for these countries should be interpreted with caution and are excluded from the figures showing the French, Dutch and UK trends.

## GFW data (spatial effort distribution and concentration) {#gfw-data}

Fishing activity data were retrieved via the Global Fishing Watch (GFW) API (gfwr v3.0) using the Events endpoint. Vessel metadata (flag state, gear type, gross tonnage) were obtained from the GFW vessel registry (https://globalfishingwatch.org; Kroodsma et al., 2018).

Recent publications have shown that the haul-based effort from GFW may not be a reliable indicator of fishing effort for trawl-based gears (Hintzen et al., 2025). Therefore, we define GFW days at sea in this report as vessel-days: for each day, each vessel is assigned to the ICES division in which it spent most of its time, based on the spatial distribution of AIS positions recorded during that day. This definition is therefore a simple presence-day metric. The effort trends derived from GFW data were found to be very different from effort trends in AER (and FDI) data. An important limitation of the GFW data is that vessels below the AIS carriage requirement threshold (typically 15 m LOA, though requirements vary by flag state and fishing area) are systematically under-represented or absent. This means that gears dominated by small inshore vessels (gillnets, pots and traps, handlines) are structurally under-counted relative to larger trawl and seine vessels, which carry AIS as a mandatory requirement. Therefore, the GFW data are used exclusively for the spatial analysis using effort density maps, spatial hotspots, and effort concentration metrics. The GFW spatial analysis covers the full period `r gfw_years_start`–`r max(study_years)`; the first year is left out of the maps because of incomplete AIS coverage.

### Kernel density estimation of spatial effort distribution

The spatial distribution of fishing effort was characterised using kernel density estimation (KDE), a standard non-parametric method for converting a set of discrete point locations into a smooth continuous surface representing effort intensity (Silverman, 1986). Fishing event coordinates were projected into a metric coordinate system (UTM Zone 30N) and a Gaussian kernel with bandwidth σ = `r sigma_all/1000` km was applied within the study area. The bandwidth is fixed across years and fleets so that changes in the density surface reflect genuine shifts in fishing distribution rather than smoothing artefacts. Land is excluded from the estimation window. For the annual maps, the resulting surface is normalised to a 0–1 scale within each year, making spatial patterns directly comparable across years regardless of differences in total effort; for absolute effort levels, the AER-based effort figures in Section \@ref(effort) should be consulted alongside the KDE maps. For the comparison before and after Brexit, the density is expressed as the share of each period's events per unit area, so that the maps do not depend on the number of years in a period or on the growth in AIS-recorded events over time. KDE is widely used in fisheries spatial analysis to identify persistent hotspots, characterise seasonal grounds and detect shifts in fleet distribution over time (Gerritsen & Lordan, 2011; Kroodsma et al., 2018).

### Fleets in the spatial analysis {#fleet-methods}

The spatial distribution of fishing effort is shown for all fleets combined and, for the comparison before and after Brexit, for the three main national fleets in the eastern Channel (`r paste(kde_flags, collapse = ", ")`). The flag state of each vessel comes from the GFW vessel registry. The comparison uses the periods `r names(brexit_periods)[1]` (before Brexit) and `r names(brexit_periods)[2]` (after the start of the EU–UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement on 1 January 2021). Because the two periods differ in length and the number of AIS-recorded events increased over time, the density in each period is expressed as the share of that period's events per unit area, normalised within each country.

### Spatial concentration metrics: Gini coefficient and top-10% cell share

Two complementary metrics were computed annually for all fleets combined on a regular `r cell_size/1000` km × `r cell_size/1000` km grid to quantify how concentrated fishing effort is in space, rather than simply where it occurs. The Gini coefficient is a well-established inequality measure, originally from economics and widely applied in fisheries spatial analysis (Greenstreet et al., 2009; Eigaard et al., 2017), that summarises the full distribution of effort across all grid cells on a scale from 0 (effort perfectly uniform across all cells) to 1 (all effort in a single cell). Values above approximately 0.7 indicate strong spatial concentration; a rising Gini over time signals progressive compression of effort into fewer areas, which may reflect displacement from previously accessible grounds, regulatory closures or increasing targeting efficiency. The top-10% cell share is a more intuitive companion metric: it expresses what percentage of total annual fishing events falls within the 10% of grid cells that were most intensively fished that year. If effort were uniform this would equal 10%; values of 40–70% are typical in concentrated demersal fisheries. Together the two metrics capture different aspects of concentration: the Gini reflects the shape of the full distribution while the top-10% share highlights the intensity of the most-fished areas. Tracking both annually allows changes in spatial footprint to be detected even when total effort remains stable.

## Literature review approach {#lit-methods}

The literature review underpinning Section \@ref(literature) is based on:

**Scientific literature** identified through targeted searches of Web of Science, Scopus and Google Scholar using the terms: *English Channel fisheries*, *Channel demersal fisheries*, *flyshoot*, *Danish seine Channel*, *beam trawl North Sea Channel*, *scallop Pecten maximus Channel*, *seabed disturbance trawl*, *AIS fishing effort*, and combinations thereof. Priority was given to peer-reviewed articles published since 2010, supplemented by earlier foundational studies where relevant (e.g. Eigaard et al., 2016a,b; Depestele et al., 2016).

**ICES working group reports** sourced from the ICES library (https://www.ices.dk), primarily:

- *Working Group on Celtic Seas Ecoregion* (WGCSE, ICES 2025a): principal source for demersal stocks in the Channel (sole, plaice, whiting, sea bass, monkfish, megrim, mullet) and for the broader ecosystem and fisheries context of 27.7.d/e.
- *Working Group on the Assessment of Demersal Stocks in the North Sea and Skagerrak* (WGNSSK, ICES 2025c): consulted for stocks with distributions spanning the Channel (e.g. plaice, dab, horse mackerel).
- *Working Group on Widely Distributed Stocks* (WGWIDE, ICES 2025e): responsible for the assessment of mackerel (*Scomber scombrus*) and horse mackerel (*Trachurus trachurus* western stock), both of which can be important bycatch species in the study area.
- *Working Group on Cephalopod Fisheries and Life History* (WGCEPH, ICES 2025d): consulted for cuttlefish (*Sepia officinalis*) and squid (*Loligo* spp., *Illex* spp.) in the Channel. WGCEPH does not produce formal TAC advice but provides the best available science on stock status and drivers of variability.

ICES advice sheets for the relevant stocks were also consulted directly.

**Official statistics and national sources** include the STECF AER (primary quantitative source for this report), Ifremer fleet and stock assessment reports, the UK Marine Management Organisation (MMO) annual sea fisheries statistics, and the Belgian ILVO annual fleet reports (ILVO, 2022). Where possible, the most recent published edition was used.

**Policy and grey literature** includes EU regulation texts, the UK–EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement fisheries annex and parliamentary reports on post-Brexit fisheries.

All quantitative claims made in the literature sections are cross-referenced with the AER and GFW results presented in Section \@ref(trends), and discrepancies or gaps are noted where they arise.


# Trends in landings and effort in the eastern Channel {#trends}

This section describes the overall trends in landings and fishing effort in `r study_area_lab`, based on the AER and MMO data (landings and effort), and the spatial patterns in fishing effort based on the GFW data.

## Landings trends {#landings}

### Landings by species during `r aer_years_start`–`r aer_years_end`

The overall landings by species in the study area during all of the years available in the AER and MMO data are shown in Figure \@ref(fig:aer-landings-top-species). The species with the highest landings are `r top_species_txt`. The main countries fishing for pelagic species (herring, horse mackerel) are the Netherlands, Germany and the UK. Scallops are mainly fished by France and the UK.

```{r aer-landings-top-species, fig.height=6, fig.cap=cap[["aer-landings-top-species"]]}

# ---- Top 20 species by total landed weight, AER + MMO, by country -------------
# Species are grouped on the harmonised code (species_code_harm), so species
# that the AER and MMO code differently (e.g. HOM/JAX) are counted together.
# Years are limited to the AER period, so all countries cover the same years.

top_years     <- aer_years_start:aer_years_end
top_countries <- unique(report_countries_combined)

top_data <- landings_combined |>
  filter(sub_reg %in% study_divisions_aer,
         year    %in% top_years) |>
  mutate(country_code = if_else(country_code %in% top_countries,
                                country_code, "Other"))

# One name per harmonised code: the most frequent name in the data
top_names <- top_data |>
  count(species_code_harm, species_name_harm, wt = live_weight_t) |>
  group_by(species_code_harm) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(species_code_harm, species_name_harm)

# Top 20 species over all countries
top_species <- top_data |>
  group_by(species_code_harm) |>
  summarise(total_t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  slice_max(total_t, n = 20) |>
  left_join(top_names, by = "species_code_harm") |>
  mutate(species_label = paste0(species_name_harm, " (", species_code_harm, ")"))

plot_top <- top_data |>
  filter(species_code_harm %in% top_species$species_code_harm) |>
  group_by(species_code_harm, country_code) |>
  summarise(total_t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(top_species |> dplyr::select(species_code_harm, species_label, species_total = total_t),
            by = "species_code_harm") |>
  mutate(species_label = fct_reorder(species_label, species_total),
         # countries ordered by their total, largest first; "Other" last
         country_code  = fct_reorder(country_code, total_t, .fun = sum, .desc = TRUE),
         country_code  = fct_relevel(country_code, "Other", after = Inf))

# Colours: flag_colours where defined, extra colours for any other country
extra_cty   <- setdiff(levels(plot_top$country_code), names(flag_colours))
cty_colours <- c(flag_colours,
                 setNames(c("#EDC948", "#9C755F", "#FF9DA7", "#499894")[seq_along(extra_cty)],
                          extra_cty))

ggplot(plot_top, aes(x = total_t / 1000, y = species_label, fill = country_code)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cty_colours, name = "Country") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.03)),
                     labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(title    = "Top 20 species by total landed weight, all gears",
       subtitle = paste0(study_area_lab, "  \u2014  ", min(top_years), "\u2013", max(top_years)),
       caption  = paste0("AER (", aer_source_lab, "); UK landings after ", aer_uk_years_end,
                         " and Channel Islands (CHI) from MMO."),
       x = "Total landed weight (1000 t)", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title      = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
        plot.caption    = element_text(size = 8, colour = "grey40")) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1))
```

Tangle (LQD) is a seaweed species harvested from the sea (*Laminaria digitata*). Common European bittersweet (GKL) is a shellfish species (*Glycymeris glycymeris*).

### Total landed weight by year, country and gear

Total landings by gear and country are shown in Figure \@ref(fig:aer-landings-total). The highest landings were in the category Other/mixed (including pelagic trawl for e.g. herring, and some fisheries for scallops). Other important gears are bottom trawl/seine (France, decreasing) and dredge (France and the UK, increasing).

```{r aer-landings-total, fig.height=6, fig.cap=cap[["aer-landings-total"]]}

# ---- Landed weight by year, gear category and country, AER + MMO --------------
gear_countries <- unique(report_countries_combined)

plot_gear <- landings_combined |>
  # remove_pelagic_anomaly() |>
  filter(country_code  %in% gear_countries,
         sub_reg       %in% study_divisions_aer,
         gear_category %in% report_gears_aer) |>
  mutate(data_source = if_else(str_detect(source, "MMO"), "MMO", "AER")) |>
  group_by(year, country_code, gear_category, data_source) |>
  summarise(live_weight_t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  complete(year, country_code, gear_category, fill = list(live_weight_t = NA_real_)) |>
  mutate(country_code  = factor(country_code,  levels = gear_countries),
         gear_category = factor(gear_category, levels = report_gears_aer))

# Colours: flag_colours where defined, extra colours for any other country
extra_cty   <- setdiff(gear_countries, names(flag_colours))
cty_colours <- c(flag_colours,
                 setNames(c("#EDC948", "#9C755F", "#FF9DA7", "#499894")[seq_along(extra_cty)],
                          extra_cty))

gear_years <- range(plot_gear$year)

ggplot(plot_gear, aes(x = year, y = live_weight_t,
                      colour = country_code, group = country_code)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = aer_uk_years_end + 0.5, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line(na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = data_source), size = 1.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cty_colours, drop = FALSE, na.value = "grey70",
                      name = "Country") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(AER = 16, MMO = 1), na.translate = FALSE,
                     name = "Source") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(gear_years[1], gear_years[2], by = 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05)),
                     labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  # facet_wrap(~gear_category, scales = "free_y") +
  facet_wrap(~gear_category) +
  labs(title    = "Landed weight by gear category and country",
       subtitle = paste0(study_area_lab, "  \u2014  AER (", aer_source_lab, ") and MMO"),
       caption  = paste0(c(paste0("Dashed line: UK landings from the AER up to ", aer_uk_years_end,
                                  ", from MMO afterwards (open points)."),
                           pelagic_anomaly_note), collapse = "\n"),
       x = "Year", y = "Landed weight (t)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text      = element_text(size = 7),
        axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.box      = "horizontal",
        plot.caption    = element_text(size = 6.5, colour = "grey40")) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1),
         shape  = guide_legend(nrow = 1))
```

### Total landed weight for Other/mixed gear {#landings-other}

The Other/mixed gear category covers a highly diverse range of fishing techniques and target species that do not fit neatly into the main AER gear categories, and its composition differs markedly by country (Figure \@ref(fig:aer-landings-species-country-groups)). The French Other/mixed landings were dominated by scallops and pelagic fish. Dutch, German and UK Other/mixed landings were almost entirely pelagic fish.

```{r aer-landings-species-country-groups, fig.height=6, fig.cap=cap[["aer-landings-species-country-groups"]]}

# ---- Other/mixed gear: landings by species group and country, AER + MMO --------
# Countries with less than min_share_pct of the Other/mixed landings are left out,
# because their bars would not be visible at this scale.
min_share_pct <- 1

om_data <- landings_combined |>
  filter(sub_reg       %in% study_divisions_aer,
         gear_category == "Other/mixed",
         country_code  %in% unique(report_countries_combined)) |>
  mutate(species_group = group_species_top(species_code_harm, species_name_harm),
         species_group = factor(species_group, levels = species_group_levels_top))

om_countries <- om_data |>
  group_by(country_code) |>
  summarise(t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * t / sum(t)) |>
  filter(pct >= min_share_pct) |>
  arrange(desc(t)) |>
  pull(country_code)

om_years <- range(om_data$year)

plot_om <- om_data |>
  filter(country_code %in% om_countries) |>
  group_by(year, country_code, species_group) |>
  summarise(live_weight_t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  complete(year = om_years[1]:om_years[2], country_code, species_group,
           fill = list(live_weight_t = 0)) |>
  mutate(country_code = factor(country_code, levels = om_countries))

ggplot(plot_om, aes(x = year, y = live_weight_t / 1000, fill = species_group)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", width = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = species_group_colours, name = "Species group", drop = TRUE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(om_years[1], om_years[2], by = 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05)),
                     labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  facet_wrap(~country_code, ncol = 2) +
  labs(title    = "Other/mixed gear: landings by species group and country",
       subtitle = paste0(study_area_lab, "  \u2014  ", om_years[1], "\u2013", om_years[2]),
       caption  = paste0("AER (", aer_source_lab, "); UK after ", aer_uk_years_end,
                         " and Channel Islands from MMO. Countries with less than ",
                         min_share_pct, "% of Other/mixed landings not shown. "),
       x = "Year", y = "Landed weight (1000 t)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.text      = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.caption    = element_text(size = 6.5, colour = "grey40")) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```

### Key species groups: landings by country

Figure \@ref(fig:aer-landings-species-country) shows the landings of the key species groups by country. Landings were dominated by pelagic fish (the Netherlands, Germany, the UK and France) and scallops (France and the UK). Roundfish and flatfish landings declined markedly. Cuttlefish and squid landings have increased but remain small relative to other landings.

